info.title: Jul admin API
info.description:
The supported, versioned external administration API.

Only the operations described here are part of the compatibility contract. The admin listener serves many other routes; they exist for the Console and may change shape in any release.

Every authenticated route requires a transport that is either TLS-terminated or bound to loopback. Cleartext non-loopback requests are refused before authentication.

Request bodies, query/header parameters, response types and errors are generated from the authoritative Go route catalog and Go wire types. This document is never hand-edited.

get.summary: What this build serves: API version, configuration schema version, compiled feature flags, the external operations available, and the ledger bounds a polling client must respect.

X-Request-ID.description: Server-minted correlation identifier for this request.

401.description: `unauthenticated` — No credential was presented, or the credential is not valid. Carries no signal about whether the addressed resource exists.

403.description:
`insecure_transport` — The request arrived in cleartext on a listener that is neither TLS-terminated nor bound to loopback, on a route that consumes an admin credential. Rejected before route lookup and before authentication.

`forbidden` — The principal is authenticated but does not hold the required permission. The check runs before the resource is looked up, so this carries no existence signal either.

429.description: `rate_limited` — The admin rate limit was exceeded. retry_after_seconds is a requirement, and is also sent as Retry-After.

500.description: `internal_error` — An unexpected server failure. The request_id correlates the response with the server log, which holds the detail this response deliberately does not.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional 8–128 byte [A-Za-z0-9_-] key, scoped to the authenticated principal and current boot. Reusing it for byte-identical input replays the recorded operation; reusing it for different input conflicts.

400.description:
`invalid_request` — The request was malformed: an unparseable body, an unknown field, a bad parameter or a missing required parameter.

`validation_failed` — The candidate configuration is not valid. Findings carry the exact configuration path that failed.

401.description: `unauthenticated` — No credential was presented, or the credential is not valid. Carries no signal about whether the addressed resource exists.

403.description:
`insecure_transport` — The request arrived in cleartext on a listener that is neither TLS-terminated nor bound to loopback, on a route that consumes an admin credential. Rejected before route lookup and before authentication.

`forbidden` — The principal is authenticated but does not hold the required permission. The check runs before the resource is looked up, so this carries no existence signal either.

409.description:
`stale_base_version` — Optimistic-concurrency failure: the configuration changed since base_version was observed.

`drift_detected` — Managed authority with an external write present on disk — including an adoption whose bytes changed under it at the verification fence.

`config_authority_read_only` — The server is in file_owned authority and does not write configuration. This is a property of the server, identical for every principal including a wildcard admin, which is why it is 409 and not 403.

`pending_restart_conflict` — A staged planned restart blocks this operation.

`restart_required` — The candidate cannot be hot-applied. The named subsystems require a restart.

`idempotency_key_reused` — The Idempotency-Key matches a recorded operation with a different request fingerprint. The recorded operation is named by its route template, never by a concrete path.

`idempotency_key_in_flight` — The Idempotency-Key matches an operation that has not reached a terminal state. Poll the named apply_id rather than retrying.

413.description: `payload_too_large` — The request body exceeded the admin body cap. The cap applies to every body-bearing /api/v1 request, not only mutations.

415.description: `unsupported_media_type` — The request Content-Type is not accepted for this operation.

429.description: `rate_limited` — The admin rate limit was exceeded. retry_after_seconds is a requirement, and is also sent as Retry-After.

500.description: `internal_error` — An unexpected server failure. The request_id correlates the response with the server log, which holds the detail this response deliberately does not.

501.description: `not_implemented` — The capability is not compiled into this build. Returned instead of 404 so a client never has to infer capability from a missing route.

504.description: `operation_timeout` — reload_timeout was exceeded before the operation reached a terminal state.

get.summary: Configuration history as safe metadata, newest first. Paginated with limit and cursor; returns no snapshot bodies. The only v1 collection that paginates, because it is the only unbounded one.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Requested page size. Omitted means 50. Syntactically valid integers below 1 are normalized to 1; values above 200 are normalized to 200. The response reports the effective limit and limit_clamped. No OpenAPI minimum/maximum is imposed because out-of-range integers are valid normalized input.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque continuation cursor returned by the previous page. Do not construct or inspect it.

ErrorCode.description:
The bounded external error-code catalogue. `code` is the machine contract; `message` is human text.

- `admin_reachability_confirmation_required` (409): The change would alter admin reachability and must be confirmed explicitly.
- `config_authority_read_only` (409): The server is in file_owned authority and does not write configuration. This is a property of the server, identical for every principal including a wildcard admin, which is why it is 409 and not 403.
- `drift_detected` (409): Managed authority with an external write present on disk — including an adoption whose bytes changed under it at the verification fence.
- `forbidden` (403): The principal is authenticated but does not hold the required permission. The check runs before the resource is looked up, so this carries no existence signal either.
- `idempotency_key_in_flight` (409): The Idempotency-Key matches an operation that has not reached a terminal state. Poll the named apply_id rather than retrying.
- `idempotency_key_reused` (409): The Idempotency-Key matches a recorded operation with a different request fingerprint. The recorded operation is named by its route template, never by a concrete path.
- `insecure_transport` (403): The request arrived in cleartext on a listener that is neither TLS-terminated nor bound to loopback, on a route that consumes an admin credential. Rejected before route lookup and before authentication.
- `internal_error` (500): An unexpected server failure. The request_id correlates the response with the server log, which holds the detail this response deliberately does not.
- `invalid_request` (400): The request was malformed: an unparseable body, an unknown field, a bad parameter or a missing required parameter.
- `not_found` (404): The addressed resource does not exist. Returned only to a caller that already holds the required permission.
- `not_implemented` (501): The capability is not compiled into this build. Returned instead of 404 so a client never has to infer capability from a missing route.
- `operation_failed` (400): A typed patch operation was rejected. The index identifies which operation in the batch failed.
- `operation_timeout` (504): reload_timeout was exceeded before the operation reached a terminal state.
- `payload_too_large` (413): The request body exceeded the admin body cap. The cap applies to every body-bearing /api/v1 request, not only mutations.
- `pending_restart_conflict` (409): A staged planned restart blocks this operation.
- `rate_limited` (429): The admin rate limit was exceeded. retry_after_seconds is a requirement, and is also sent as Retry-After.
- `restart_required` (409): The candidate cannot be hot-applied. The named subsystems require a restart.
- `stale_base_version` (409): Optimistic-concurrency failure: the configuration changed since base_version was observed.
- `storage_unavailable` (503): The configuration or history store cannot be read or written.
- `unauthenticated` (401): No credential was presented, or the credential is not valid. Carries no signal about whether the addressed resource exists.
- `unsupported_media_type` (415): The request Content-Type is not accepted for this operation.
- `validation_failed` (400): The candidate configuration is not valid. Findings carry the exact configuration path that failed.
